title: Optimize Console: recommendation preview timeline and safe apply chronicle
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a cohesive Console experience for Redwood Optimize that surfaces automated batching and caching recommendations, previews diffs for proposed runtime config changes, and provides a tamper-evident apply/rollback audit trail. The goal is to give engineers and platform owners confidence to accept cost-saving recommendations with minimal risk and clear rollback paths.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation cards are available in the Optimize dashboard showing estimated token savings, latency impact (p50/p95), and confidence score for each suggestion.
Clicking a recommendation opens a diff preview modal that shows exact config changes (JSON/toml-like) with inline rationale and sample request before/after latency and cost simulations.
Users can stage multiple recommendation changes and preview the combined diff, with highlighted potential conflicts (e.g., incompatible batching + kv-cache policy).
Apply flow requires a canary option (percentage or route selector), immutable audit entry containing user id, timestamp, before/after config, and a rollback action that records reason and initiator.
All apply/rollback actions surface in a timeline UI (Apply History) with search/filter by user, config key, model, or time window, and link to related deployment/PR when available.

Telemetry events emitted for preview_open, preview_apply_attempt, apply_success, apply_failed, rollback_requested, rollback_completed, and feedback_submitted. Schemas documented in GH issue and analytics dashboard shows top N savings realized.
Role-based access control: only users with 'Optimize:Apply' permission see the apply button; read-only users can comment and stage suggestions.
Retention policy: audit entries retained for 1 year by default, exportable as CSV/JSON from the Apply History page.
notes: Trade-offs: showing exact generated config increases clarity but raises exposure risk for secrets/keys; we'll redact values and show structural diffs only.
Performance: server-side diff generation should be cached for repeated preview requests to avoid heavy compile runs; add a short TTL (5m).
Compliance: for Private customers with strict audit requirements, we will add an optional signed-audit artifact (HMAC) that can be shipped to customer S3/HSM.
